solution: Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(\cos 2x) = -2\sin 2x\), an antiderivative of \(\sin 2x\) is \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\cos 2x\). Thus \(\int \sin 2x\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}\cos 2x + C\).
Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sin 3x) = 3\cos 3x\), an antiderivative of \(\cos 3x\) is \(\tfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x\). Thus \(\int \cos 3x\,dx = \frac{1}{3}\sin 3x + C\).
Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(e^{2x}) = 2e^{2x}\), an antiderivative of \(e^{2x}\) is \(\tfrac{1}{2}e^{2x}\). Thus \(\int e^{2x}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x} + C\).
Note \(\frac{d}{dx}\!\left[(ax+b)^3\right] = 3a(ax+b)^2\), so an antiderivative of \((ax+b)^2\) is \(\frac{(ax+b)^3}{3a}\). Thus \(\int (ax+b)^2\,dx = \frac{(ax+b)^3}{3a} + C\).
Integrate term by term: \(\int \sin 2x\,dx = -\tfrac{1}{2}\cos 2x\) and \(\int e^{3x}\,dx = \tfrac{1}{3}e^{3x}\). Hence \(\int (\sin 2x - 4e^{3x})\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}\cos 2x - \frac{4}{3}e^{3x} + C\).
Integrate term by term: \(\int (4e^{3x} + 1)\,dx = 4\cdot\tfrac{1}{3}e^{3x} + x = \frac{4}{3}e^{3x} + x + C\).
Expand first: \(x^2\left(1 - \frac{1}{x^2}\right) = x^2 - 1\). Then \(\int (x^2 - 1)\,dx = \frac{x^3}{3} - x + C\).
Integrate term by term: \(\int (ax^2 + bx + c)\,dx = \frac{ax^3}{3} + \frac{bx^2}{2} + cx + C\).
Integrate term by term: \(\int (2x^2 + e^x)\,dx = \frac{2x^3}{3} + e^x + C\).
Expand: \(\left(\sqrt{x} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)^2 = x - 2 + \frac{1}{x}\). Then \(\int \left(x - 2 + \frac{1}{x}\right) dx = \frac{x^2}{2} - 2x + \log|x| + C\).
Divide through by \(x^2\): \(\frac{x^3 + 5x^2 - 4}{x^2} = x + 5 - 4x^{-2}\). Then \(\int \left(x + 5 - 4x^{-2}\right) dx = \frac{x^2}{2} + 5x + \frac{4}{x} + C\).
Integrate term by term: \(\int (2x - 3\cos x + e^x)\,dx = x^2 - 3\sin x + e^x + C\).
Integrate term by term, using \(\int \sqrt{x}\,dx = \tfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\): \(\int (2x^2 - 3\sin x + 5\sqrt{x})\,dx = \frac{2x^3}{3} + 3\cos x + \frac{10}{3}x^{3/2} + C\).

Expand: \(\sec x\,(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x\). Since \(\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x\) and \(\int \sec x \tan x\,dx = \sec x\), we get \(\int \sec x\,(\sec x + \tan x)\,dx = \tan x + \sec x + C\).
Write \(\frac{\sec^2 x}{\csc^2 x} = \sec^2 x \cdot \sin^2 x = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\). Then \(\int (\sec^2 x - 1)\,dx = \tan x - x + C\).
Split: \(\frac{2 - 3\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x - 3\,\frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x - 3\sec x \tan x\). Then \(\int (2\sec^2 x - 3\sec x \tan x)\,dx = 2\tan x - 3\sec x + C\).
Use \(e^{k\log x} = x^{k}\): the integrand becomes \(\frac{x^5 - x^4}{x^3 - x^2} = \frac{x^4(x-1)}{x^2(x-1)} = x^2\). Then \(\int x^2\,dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C\).
